inspection.source_name: Factory floor with marked pedestrian walkway
inspection.analysis_provider: Recorded vision review + YOLO object-detection annotations
inspection.analysis_summary: The clip shows an indoor factory floor with large machinery on the left and a wide central aisle. A green pedestrian route bordered by yellow lines runs along the right side. Across the reviewed timestamps, workers are visible walking or standing in the central aisle outside that marked route. The recording does not clearly establish whether the route is mandatory for every activity. No clear spill, fire, sparks, major dust plume, moving vehicle, or machine-guarding defect is supported by the supplied frames.

events.title: WORKERS POSITIONED OUTSIDE MARKED GREEN PEDESTRIAN LANE
events.visible_evidence: A worker is visible in the central concrete aisle rather than inside the green pedestrian route bordered by yellow floor lines on the right side of the factory floor.
events.why_it_matters: Walking outside a marked pedestrian route may increase the chance of interaction with nearby machinery, material movement, or vehicle traffic. The footage alone does not establish the site rule or whether the movement was authorised.
events.recommended_follow_up: Confirm that the green/yellow marking is the designated pedestrian route for this area, then review the task and reinforce the site traffic-separation procedure where applicable.

models.reconstruction_note: The supplied Ling 3.2 Flash benchmark request did not complete: OpenRouter returned HTTP 429 (rate limit). The provided Ling-named annotated MP4 is byte-for-byte identical to the main annotated video, so it is not independent evidence of a Ling model response. The six event timestamps and labels below are reconstructed from the main inspection timeline, not returned by Ling. YOLO alignment (5/6) is inferred from the main annotation overlays; cross-model agreement (6/6) is an approximate same-event comparison against the two available NVIDIA model outputs. Latency (32.45s) is borrowed from the Ling run in the existing first-video demo, tokens (12,079 input + 1,120 output) are estimated, and $0.000000 cost is assumed for a free route rather than provider-reported. Consequently the 83.5/100 score and EST. BETTER rank are illustrative estimates and must not be presented as measured Ling performance.

weights.label: YOLO subject alignment
weights.description: Share of eligible subject findings linked to a matching YOLO subject.

weights.label: Cross-model corroboration
weights.description: Share of findings also reported by another selected model within a ±5-second time window.

weights.label: Structured output completeness
weights.description: Share of findings with a non-empty title, issue category, and timestamp.

weights.label: Response speed
weights.description: Relative runtime; the fastest available model receives the full score.

weights.label: Token efficiency
weights.description: Relative token use; the lowest total token count receives the full score.

weights.label: Cost efficiency
weights.description: Provider-reported cost when available; the reconstructed Ling value is an explicit assumption.

speed.basis: Estimated using the 32.45-second Ling latency recorded in the existing first-video demo; not measured for this clip.

tokens.basis: Estimated output volume for six short findings; input tokens approximated from the same run-level prompt/frame payload size shown for the other models.

cost.basis: Assumed zero for a free route; no provider usage record or billing receipt was supplied.

comparison.method_note: BEST, BETTER, and GOOD are relative positions in this saved comparison, not ground-truth accuracy labels. Cross-model agreement is a consistency signal, not proof of correctness.
